context: Hourly invariant checker change (TEST FIXTURE: deliberately buggy sample)

deterministic_findings.title: SQL statement built by string formatting/concatenation
deterministic_findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries / bound parameters for every value.

deterministic_findings.title: Possible hardcoded secret in added code
deterministic_findings.recommendation: Move the value to the secret store / environment and rotate it if it was ever real.

deterministic_findings.title: Notification/alert added with no dedup, cooldown, or state guard visible in the change
deterministic_findings.recommendation: Gate repeated alerts on a persisted state/signature so a persistent condition cannot flood recipients — send on change, suppress repeats, re-alert on recovery.

reviewer_reports.summary: The change introduces critical production risks: SQL injection via string interpolation, data loss from unconditional job deletion, credential exposure, and unbounded alert flooding without deduplication or cooldown.

findings.title: SQL injection via string interpolation
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries with placeholders instead of f-strings for SQL execution.

findings.title: Unconditional job deletion without dedup or confirmation
findings.evidence: for v in violations: db.execute(f"DELETE FROM jobs WHERE id = {v.job_id}")
findings.recommendation: Add a deduplication guard, a confirmation step, or a soft-delete flag; never delete jobs unconditionally in a health checker.

findings.title: Hardcoded SMTP password in source
findings.recommendation: Remove the hardcoded credential; pull from a secret manager or environment variable at runtime.

findings.title: Alert flood without dedup/cooldown
findings.recommendation: Add dedup logic (e.g., track last-alert timestamp per violation) or a cooldown to prevent alert floods during repeated invariant checks.

findings.title: Violation count no longer returned meaningfully
findings.recommendation: Ensure the return value reflects the intended state after deletions, or remove the return if it is no longer needed.
